collection.description: A fishing family from the next bay came through last week, heading for the big islands to the south.

ask.text:
A fishing family from the next bay came through last week, heading for the big islands to the south. This morning, in the canoe shed, (subject) finds a basket that wasn't there before, tucked behind the paddles. In it is a baby, perhaps three months old, asleep, with a full gourd of milk beside it and a string of the family's red beads round its ankle.
There is a message too, scratched on a piece of bark by someone who has only just learned to write: "Too many mouths. Please." Their canoe is long gone. The bay is empty to the horizon.
Should (subject) take the baby home, or take it to the {@chief}?

c1o1.text: (subject) keeps the bark message, folded in a cloth. When the baby is old enough, (subject) will show it to (subject.him/her), and explain that (subject.his/her) family loved (subject.him/her) enough to find (subject.him/her) a home where there was food. Until then, (subject) gets up at night, and walks the beach with (subject.him/her), and learns all the songs.

text_only.reason: the word in the owner's story; what changes in the game is the ending's own EFFECT line (the ledger), so this word alone changes nothing

c1o2.text: (friend) reads the message twice, and then sits down and holds out (friend.his/her) arms without a word. The baby is passed over, and frowns at (friend) too, and then, slowly, smiles. "Well," says (friend). "That's that decided." They raise the baby together, and wear a red bead each, to match.

c1.text: (subject) picks up the basket, bark message and all. The baby wakes, looks up at (subject.him/her) with a frown, and starts to suck its fist thoughtfully...

c2o1.text: "Who will take this child?" asks the {@chief}. There's a silence. Then (healer), who has a baby of (subject.his/her) own and milk enough for two, stands up. "Give (subject.him/her) here," (subject.he/she) says. The baby grows up in the healers' hut, with a milk-brother and a lot of very bossy healers.

c2o2.text: "Who will take this child?" asks the {@chief}, and before (subject) knows it, (subject.he/she) is standing up. The village cheers. Every family brings something that night: a mat, a little blanket, a carved spoon. (subject) ends up with more baby things than one baby could ever use, and passes them on to every new baby in the village for years.

c2.text: (subject) carries the basket to the {@chief}'s hut. The {@chief} reads the message, sighs, and calls the whole village together at the cooking fire...
